chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafur, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is there anything for the woman from the wergild (blood money) of her husband, and is there anything for the man from the wergild of his wife?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, so long as one of the two has not killed the other.'

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا الْآخَرَ: One of the two the other
key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or wergild paid for homicide or injury

ai.seo_question: Does a wife inherit blood money from her husband if he is killed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that spouses inherit each other's blood money (diyah) as distinct assets, provided the death was not caused by the other spouse, thereby preventing the 'killing excludes inheritance' rule from applying to the marital bond. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that diyah is a separate financial right distinct from the estate, ensuring the surviving spouse retains their share even if the other spouse caused the death. It underscores the principle that the killer is excluded from inheriting the victim's estate but does not lose the right to inherit the victim's specific compensation for death.
